rice.name: Rice
rice.description: Rice is a staple cereal crop in India, requiring warm temperatures, high humidity, and abundant standing water during vegetative stages.
rice.growing_season: Kharif (June - November) / Boro in certain regions
rice.soil_preference: Deep clayey loam or silty clay soils with good water-holding capacity and impermeable subsoil.
care_tips: Maintain 3-5 cm water depth during tillering and flowering stages.
Apply nitrogen in 3 split doses: basal, active tillering, and panicle initiation.
Incorporate zinc sulphate (25 kg/ha) if deficiency symptoms (khaira disease) appear.
Drain field 10-14 days before harvest to facilitate uniform grain ripening.
rice.harvest_indicators: Golden yellow panicles with over 80% grains turned straw-colored.
rice.major_states: West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Bihar

maize.name: Maize (Corn)
maize.description: Maize is a versatile high-yield crop known as the 'Queen of Cereals', used for food, livestock feed, and industrial starch.
maize.soil_preference: Deep, fertile, well-drained sandy loam to silty loam rich in organic matter. Highly sensitive to waterlogging.
care_tips: Ensure furrow irrigation and ridge planting to avoid standing water around stalks.
Tasseling and silking are critical moisture-sensitive stages.
Apply phosphorus and potassium as basal doses, split nitrogen at knee-high and tasseling stages.
Monitor for Fall Armyworm (FAW) early in vegetative growth.
maize.harvest_indicators: Husks turn brownish and dry; kernel moisture drops to around 15-20%.
maize.major_states: Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Bihar

chickpea.name: Chickpea (Bengal Gram)
chickpea.description: Chickpea is India's most important cool-season pulse crop, enriching soil nitrogen through symbiotic Rhizobium root nodules.
chickpea.soil_preference: Well-drained light to medium black soils and loamy soils with good subsoil drainage.
care_tips: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium and PSB cultures prior to sowing.
Avoid heavy nitrogen fertilization as it delays flowering and encourages vegetative excess.
Provide light irrigation at branching and pod development stages; avoid overwatering at flowering.
Watch for pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera) and deploy pheromone traps.
chickpea.harvest_indicators: Leaves turn yellowish and dry; pods rattle when gently shaken.
chickpea.major_states: Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat

kidneybeans.name: Kidney Beans (Rajma)
kidneybeans.description: Rajma is a high-protein legume crop commonly cultivated in northern hilly and plateau regions in mild cool climates.
kidneybeans.growing_season: Kharif in hilly regions / Rabi in central plains
kidneybeans.soil_preference: Rich, well-aerated sandy loam or alluvial soils with high organic matter content.
care_tips: Unlike other pulses, kidney beans fix less atmospheric nitrogen; provide adequate starter nitrogen.
Stake trailing varieties or choose bush types for mechanized field maintenance.
Keep soil moist but never stagnant; susceptible to root rot in poorly drained soils.
Harvest promptly when pods lose green color to avoid shattering.
kidneybeans.harvest_indicators: Pods turn yellow-straw colored and seeds harden inside the pods.
kidneybeans.major_states: Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Maharashtra

pigeonpeas.name: Pigeon Peas (Arhar / Toor)
pigeonpeas.description: Pigeon pea is an essential source of protein in Indian diet (dal). It is drought-hardy and possesses a deep taproot that breaks hard subsoil layers.
pigeonpeas.soil_preference: Deep, well-drained loam or clay loam soils. Sensitive to saline and alkaline conditions.
care_tips: Excellent companion for intercropping with cotton, sorghum, or soybean.
Provide protective irrigation during flowering and pod development if dry spell exceeds 15 days.
Pruning or nipping of terminal shoots around 40-50 days promotes profuse lateral branching.
Apply sulfur-containing single superphosphate (SSP) to improve protein synthesis.
pigeonpeas.harvest_indicators: 75-80% pods turn brown and dry on the plants.
pigeonpeas.major_states: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat

mothbeans.name: Moth Beans (Matki)
mothbeans.description: Moth bean is an exceptionally drought-tolerant arid legume that thrives in low rainfall and sandy soil, preventing soil erosion.
mothbeans.soil_preference: Light sandy to sandy loam soils with rapid drainage.
care_tips: Ideal crop for rainfed arid and semi-arid conditions where other crops fail.
Spreads dense vegetative cover that acts as a live mulch conserving soil moisture.
Requires minimal synthetic fertilizers due to robust nitrogen-fixing nodulation.
Harvest early in the morning when pods have dew moisture to minimize shattering loss.
mothbeans.harvest_indicators: Pods change from yellow-green to brown; plants begin shedding leaves.

mungbean.name: Mung Bean (Green Gram)
mungbean.description: Mung bean is a fast-maturing pulse that fits well into crop rotations, enriching soil organic matter and nitrogen.
mungbean.soil_preference: Well-drained fertile loam or sandy loam. Avoid saline and waterlogged ground.
care_tips: Seed treatment with Thiram and Rhizobium increases germination vigor.
Give one light irrigation at pre-flowering and one at early pod filling.
Control yellow mosaic virus (YMV) by managing whitefly vector populations.
Pick mature black pods in 2-3 flushes if indeterminate variety is grown.
mungbean.harvest_indicators: 80% of pods turn dark brown to blackish.
mungbean.major_states: Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu

blackgram.name: Black Gram (Urad)
blackgram.description: Black gram is a nutrient-dense pulse rich in iron, protein, and dietary fiber, often rotated with rice in paddy fallows.
blackgram.growing_season: Kharif, Spring, and Rabi in southern regions
blackgram.soil_preference: Heavy soils, loamy or clayey soils with adequate moisture retention capacity.
care_tips: Broadcasting in standing rice crop prior to harvest (relay cropping) saves tillage costs.
Apply 2% DAP foliar spray at flowering stage to enhance pod set.
Keep field free from weeds for the first 30 days.
Harvest whole plants when leaves fall and pods become dry and black.
blackgram.harvest_indicators: Pods turn glossy black and brittle.
blackgram.major_states: Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra

lentil.name: Lentil (Masoor)
lentil.description: Lentil is a resilient winter legume cultivated widely across the Gangetic plains, requiring cool growth conditions.
lentil.soil_preference: Alluvial, sandy loam to clay loam soils with neutral to slightly acidic pH.
care_tips: Perform seed treatment with biofertilizers and fungicide to curb collar rot.
Tolerates moderate dry spells; one irrigation at flowering is sufficient if rain is deficient.
Sensitive to waterlogging, ensure beds have mild drainage incline.
Harvest promptly when bottom pods dry to avoid grain shattering.
lentil.harvest_indicators: Leaves turn yellow, lower pods dry to yellowish brown.
lentil.major_states: Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Rajasthan

pomegranate.name: Pomegranate (Anar)
pomegranate.description: Pomegranate is a commercially valuable fruit crop that thrives in semi-arid environments with hot dry summers and mild winters.
pomegranate.growing_season: Perennial (Bahar flowering: Ambe, Mrig, or Hasta bahar)
pomegranate.soil_preference: Well-drained deep loamy soil or light alluvial soil with good aeration. Can tolerate slightly alkaline and rocky ground.
care_tips: Prune crisscross and dead branches annually to maintain open center canopy for sunlight penetration.
Regulate watering strictly during fruit enlargement to prevent fruit cracking.
Apply organic manure (FYM 20-30 kg/plant) along with micronutrients (Boron, Zinc).
Monitor for bacterial blight (Teliya) and fruit borer; bag developing fruits.
pomegranate.harvest_indicators: Rind turns characteristic reddish-yellow, fruits produce metallic sound when tapped.
pomegranate.major_states: Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan

banana.name: Banana
banana.description: Banana is a high-volume, rapid-growing tropical fruit demanding abundant nutrients, ample moisture, and sheltered warm conditions.
banana.water_requirement: Very High (1500 - 2000 mm regular drip supply)
banana.soil_preference: Deep, fertile, moisture-retentive alluvial or clayey loam rich in potassium and organic matter.
care_tips: Provide propping (bamboo or rope support) as bunches emerge to prevent lodging from wind.
Desuckering: remove unwanted daughter suckers regularly, keeping one follower sucker for ratoon.
Heavy potassium feeder: apply muriate of potash (MOP) in split doses during bunch formation.
Cover emerging bunches with perforated polythene sleeves to protect skin quality.
banana.harvest_indicators: Angles of banana fingers become rounded and top leaves turn dry.
banana.major_states: Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh
